top_candidates.original_title: I said no and Apple said yes
top_candidates.generated_headline: Apple Intelligence Overrides User Refusal, Re-enabling Local Models Post-Update
top_candidates.summary: An OS update quietly strips away prior user opt-outs, re-enabling local intelligence features and consuming gigabytes of disk space without consent. The tradeoff is an operating system that treats user preference as a temporary suggestion rather than a hard boundary.

top_candidates.original_title: Data-only attacks are easier than you think (2024)
top_candidates.generated_headline: The Silent Vulnerability of State: Why Data-Only Attacks Demand a Reversal in Memory Discipline
top_candidates.summary: Recent analyses show that compromising software state without altering control flow remains alarmingly straightforward, bypassing traditional hardening techniques. The primary risk lies in our over-reliance on automated mitigations while the fundamental discipline of data layout continues to erode.
